correctness.rationale: Reconstructed all quantifiers and conventions: five distinct unit-circle samples determine the degree-two Hermitian Laurent polynomial; the kernel is the explicit four-real-parameter subspace. The three off-circle equations are rank three because three distinct points determine one generalized circle. For its unique kernel generator, determinant equals (t-a)(|u|^2-at), with strictly positive second factor for both ordinary circles and lines. The rank-two lifting criterion gives both directions even with zero coefficients. Two-dimensional Hermitian kernels for at most seven samples necessarily contain a nonzero singular indefinite element by determinant oddness, proving optimal cardinality. The accompanying checker verifies 85 exact symbolic and geometric assertions, including explicit positive and negative anchors; they support rather than replace the universal proof.

value.rationale: The 5+3 sampling pattern is a natural hybrid of optimal trigonometric autocorrelation sampling and minimal off-circle phase disambiguation. The full necessary-and-sufficient condition is the computable orthogonality invariant of three arbitrary complex anchor points, including both straight-line and circular loci, and the proof simultaneously establishes a global eight-measurement lower bound. This provides a complete and geometrically meaningful classification of an infinite family of optimal-size designs; not just one finite computation. No stability or higher-degree conclusion is asserted.
